$comment: Recommended MCP suite. This file is the single declaration of what a correctly
configured workstation looks like: which servers belong to the suite, how each one
is launched, which settings it needs, and where each setting legitimately lives.
It is a baseline for auditing, not a lock: `isc-ai mcp audit` compares the three
clients against it and reports drift; nothing is written unless you ask for it.
credentials.scope decides where a value is read from and written to:
project  <project>/.iris-mcp/  - differs per deployment (IRIS namespaces, CCR)
global   ~/.iris-mcp/          - one per person (Jira token, Perforce identity)
Secret values never go in a committable file: config.json holds {env:VAR}
references, secrets.json holds the literals and is gitignored.
aliases lists the names these servers are known by in existing configurations, so
the audit can tell 'registered under another name' apart from 'missing'.
Suite Manifest Install Metadata: a server's (or client's) optional 'install' block
declares how its runtime dependency is obtained and pinned. Fields: manager, argv
(the literal recipe `isc-ai mcp audit` re-derives its checks from - this same argv
is what a later 'isc-ai update' command runs, unchanged, so it must stay the real
command and nothing else), pin (the version/tag), pinned (true once adopted, false
for a recorded-but-not-yet-applied candidate; pin_reason explains why), and the
optional commit field described below. This block only ever informs audit output;
declaring or changing it never installs, upgrades, or writes anything by itself.
Integrity model differs by source kind (decision: distribution-channel):
git-sourced (argv runs `... git+<url>@<tag>`, e.g. isc-ai's own extensions via
`uv tool install git+https://.../<repo>.git@<tag>`): the pin IS the tag, and the
only additional integrity check possible is an expected 40-hex commit SHA in
'commit', because a git checkout has no package/wheel checksum to verify against.
A declared tag with no 'commit' is reported (INSTALL_COMMIT_MISSING, warning) so a
moved/re-tagged ref is never installed silently; never invent a commit SHA for a
tag that has not actually been cut yet - leave it absent and let the finding fire
until the real release tagging happens.
registry-sourced (npm/uvx/npx pins like markitdown/playwright below): pin/pinned
drift detection (VERSION_UNPINNED, INSTALL_PIN_MISMATCH) is the whole check for
this source kind today. A package/wheel checksum for these is a deliberate
deferral, not an oversight - registries already provide their own integrity
(npm's package-lock/uv's resolver), and inventing a checksum here would just be a
second, unmaintained copy of a number the manager itself already verifies.
The AI clients the suite configures. Paths use placeholders resolved at runtime:
{home}, {config_home} (XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config), {appdata}, {project}.
install is a recipe, never a default action: the audit reports the command and the
package manager it needs, and running it requires --apply plus a confirmation.
Installing a client is the only thing in this CLI that touches the system outside
configuration files, so it stays explicit and one client at a time.

config.write_scope_reason: One user-level registration serves every project: the servers that need per-project data discover it themselves from the working directory.

vscode.summary: Visual Studio Code with MCP support.

config.notes: Secrets use the native `inputs` array with password:true, so the value is prompted once and stored by VS Code instead of sitting in the file.
config.write_scope_reason: User level only. A workspace mcp.json would register the same servers a second time and VS Code would run both.

config.notes: The global file also carries per-directory overrides under projects.<path>.mcpServers, which is where stale entries survive unnoticed. Enabling and disabling happens through projects.<path>.enabledMcpjsonServers / disabledMcpjsonServers.
config.write_scope_reason: The project .mcp.json is the file meant to be shared with the repository; the global file holds unrelated state and is never rewritten.

intersystems-iris.summary: IRIS/TrakCare tools with CCR-aware write gates (this package).
intersystems-iris.notes: Site policy and server connections are not settings of this entry: they live in .iris-mcp/config.json and ~/.iris-mcp/servers.json.

perforce-mcp-server.notes: Replaces the versioned absolute path of the 1.x binary: the 2.0.0 entry point is installed on PATH. P4CLIENT is per project because the workspace maps one deployment.

atlassian-cloud.summary: Jira Cloud plus optional Confluence (Cloud or Server/Data Center).
atlassian-cloud.notes: Jira is required; Confluence is optional and has its own settings because it may live on another instance with other credentials. A CONFLUENCE_URL outside *.atlassian.net is Server/Data Center and needs a personal access token in CONFLUENCE_PERSONAL_TOKEN: the Jira Cloud API token is not accepted there. The ISC Confluence (usconfluence.iscinternal.com) is reachable only over the Cisco Secure Client VPN; without it DNS fails and only the Confluence tools are missing, Jira keeps working. Confluence Cloud with its own basic-auth credentials (CONFLUENCE_USERNAME/CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN) is intentionally not declared; add those settings if a site needs it. The Claude entry named 'jira' uses ATLASSIAN_* names for the Jira values; the audit reports that as a naming drift, not as a second server. The version is pinned on purpose so a new release never runs with your token unreviewed: bump it explicitly.

context7.notes: The hosted endpoint is the recommended form: no npm package to pin and no API key to store. A local npx entry for the same server is a duplicate, not a second server.

markitdown.summary: Convert documents and URLs to Markdown.
markitdown.notes: Version pinned on purpose: an unpinned entry changes behaviour without a change on your side.

playwright.summary: Drive a real browser for UI verification.
playwright.notes: The only entry of the suite that is not pinned. Pinning it is recommended once a version is settled; the audit reports @latest as an advisory, not an error.

install.pin_reason: no version has been evaluated yet

out_of_suite.$comment: Entries found in the wild that the suite does not manage. Reported so they are a decision, not a surprise.
out_of_suite.odoo-dev-mcp: Runs `uv run <gist URL>`: fetches and executes remote code on every start. Out of the suite until it is vendored or pinned to a reviewed artifact.
